correctness.rationale: The exact result follows from the already published canonical one-point model construction: for input phi its candidate finite generator G(Delta) is a subset of the source Sub*(neg phi), polynomial in syntax length. Membership in cl_Lambda(G) for a queried box subformula can be decided by saturation restricted to the subformulas of G union {psi,top}, as Nishimura explicitly states in Corollary 3.14; this finite set has polynomial cardinality, and each monotone rule M/C/N/K adds each relevant formula only once, so O(poly(|phi|)) rounds/checks. Thus a guessed one-point model verifies SAT in polynomial time. Classical SAT and tautology embed as box-free fragments; negation transfers SAT to invalidity and strong completeness to derivability. Unrestricted C-closure can be infinite but is never claimed finite. All 16 systems and both modal-free lower bounds are covered. Correctness does NOT make this corollary original.
